### acqagent/far-collector — FAR Overhaul deviation collector and versioned evidence pipeline
- URL: https://github.com/acqagent/far-collector
- Exact commit / revision: `40789a073134a484b2e4a5a2398629b067da0eea`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: strong / Master contender
- Concrete capability: Functional acquisition.gov FAR Overhaul collector that deterministically crawls the official deviation guide, downloads agency class-deviation PDFs, preserves raw HTML/PDF artifacts, extracts Part 52 provisions/clauses plus agency/deviation/title/scope/effective-date fields, normalizes dates, stores the corpus in DuckDB, exports Excel, and supports cron-safe incremental discovery/extraction. The latest repair commit also fixed manifest regeneration and LLM truncation bugs and added deterministic parser tests/CI.
- Rare / undernoticed value: This directly attacks CaptureBrief's hardest rule-currency gap: operational FAR applicability during the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul is spread across many agency deviation PDFs rather than a single codified source. The collector distinguishes source acquisition from derived extraction and intentionally leaves unresolvable effective dates NULL rather than inventing dates.
- Likely buyer / user: Federal capture/proposal teams, compliance analysts, acquisition counsel/support contractors, GovCon intelligence vendors.
- Painful problem: A solicitation can cite apparently familiar FAR text while an agency class deviation has changed, reserved, replaced, or time-bounded the controlling rule. Manual tracking across hundreds of PDFs is labor-intensive and easy to miss.
- Monetization mechanism: Premium CaptureBrief compliance/readiness layer; managed deviation-monitor service; fixed-price solicitation rule-currency diagnostic.
- Likely first paid wedge: Given a solicitation agency/date/clause set, return the codified FAR baseline plus all potentially controlling agency deviations, effective-date evidence, source PDF/link and an explicit unresolved/conflict state.
- Build-time / data advantage: High; plausibly saves multiple engineer/domain months in guide crawling, PDF collection, effective-date normalization, manifest reconciliation, incremental refresh, local structured extraction and regression testing.
- Evidence inspected: repository metadata; latest merge and repair commits; README architecture/run/output sections; `db.py` schema including URL status/content hashes and FAR clause/deviation tables; incremental/hash-dedupe behavior described in commit history; deterministic parser/test additions.
- Public license / rights: No repository-wide public software license was detected at the inspected revision. Under the user's standing assertion, repository-owned code/content is treated as separately commercially permitted for product analysis. The underlying acquisition.gov federal documents remain separately sourced government material; model weights/dependencies retain their own terms.
- Reuse classification: Working assumption permits repository-owned code use; production legal conclusions must still bind to the official source PDF/page and current solicitation, not to an LLM-derived extraction alone.
- Why non-obvious: Only a few stars and a local-LLM collector framing hide an unusually complete moving-rule ingestion pipeline built specifically around current FAR Overhaul deviations.
- Combination opportunities: `GSA/GSA-Acquisition-FAR` structured DITA baseline + `cliwant/mcp-sam-gov` exact eCFR/prescription semantics + this collector's agency-deviation corpus + CivicProof-style hash/locatable-support gate = much stronger clause applicability evidence.
- Value score: A 5/5; B 5/5; C 5/5; D 5/5; E 5/5; F 4/5 = **29/30**. F reflects absent public repo license even though separate commercial permission is the standing working assumption.
- Next action: Build a deterministic deviation applicability index keyed by agency, FAR Part/clause, deviation number, source URL/hash, issued/effective date, supersession state and extraction confidence; benchmark it on the 10-live-solicitation set and manually verify every positive hit.

### biglocalnews/sync-fed-contracts — FPDS termination/cancellation event intelligence
- URL: https://github.com/biglocalnews/sync-fed-contracts
- Exact commit / revision: `3d6fd0ff1dc963dbc06ec7fa467504adb36cf905`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: strong
- Concrete capability: Working daily FPDS extraction pipeline that queries modification reason codes E/F/K/N/X, persists day-by-reason JSON, incrementally skips already collected files, and publishes a curated cancellation dataset. Its documented normalized fields connect PIID, solicitation ID, modification number, agency, UEI-era vendor identity fields, action date, action obligation, requirement description, PSC, business attributes and FPDS source URLs.
- Rare / undernoticed value: Contract termination/cancellation/closeout modifications are a different intelligence surface from normal award history. They can reveal incumbent disruption, program contraction, legal cancellation, closeout or potential future recompete signals that are invisible in a simple 'who won' view. The project also documents exact FPDS field-to-USAspending/SAM relationships and nuances such as zero-dollar terminations and financial adjustments occurring in separate modifications.
- Likely buyer / user: Capture/BD teams, competitive-intelligence analysts, subcontractors targeting displaced work, federal-market consultants, investigative/data teams.
- Painful problem: Teams monitor new solicitations and awards but often miss material lifecycle events on existing contracts; manually interpreting FPDS modification codes and linking them back to award/solicitation/vendor lineage is tedious.
- Monetization mechanism: Recurring incumbent-instability/recompete signal feed inside CaptureBrief; fixed-price market-change diagnostic by agency/NAICS/PSC; managed alerting for customer target accounts.
- Likely first paid wedge: For a customer's target agencies/competitors, surface new E/F/N/X termination events, verify PIID/modification/UEI in USAspending, link the originating solicitation where possible, and explain whether the event is genuine termination, closeout or ambiguous.
- Build-time / data advantage: High domain compression in FPDS modification semantics, dedupe, field mappings and operational edge cases; roughly 1–2+ months to recreate and validate credibly.
- Evidence inspected: README; actual Apache-2.0 LICENSE; `sync-fed-contracts.py` day/reason query loop using `fpdsRequest`; commit history showing incremental-progress and fetch-logic repairs; `highlighted_columns.md` mappings for PIID, solicitation ID, modification number, action obligation, legal business name, funding/contracting agencies and reason codes.
- Public license / rights: Apache-2.0 for repository code. FPDS/USAspending/SAM source data retain their own federal-source semantics; Big Local News derived crosswalks/exports require their own terms check if redistributed. User-asserted separate commercial permission independently covers repository-owned code/content.
- Reuse classification: Reusable. Never infer 'recompete' or contractor distress solely from a termination code; classify the reason, inspect the transaction lineage and verify current award status.
- Why non-obvious: An 8-star journalism/data repo is not marketed as GovCon intelligence infrastructure, but its curated cancellation semantics are commercially useful capture signals.
- Combination opportunities: `dherincx92/fpds` ingestion + this modification taxonomy + official DATA Act/USAspending PIID/referenced-IDV identity + CaptureBrief incumbent history can produce a lifecycle-change signal unavailable from opportunity feeds alone.
- Value score: A 4/5; B 4/5; C 4/5; D 5/5; E 5/5; F 5/5 = **27/30**.
- Next action: Backtest E/F/N/X events against 100 USAspending awards and subsequent SAM opportunities; estimate how often they precede recompetes or materially alter incumbent assumptions, keeping K/closeout and ambiguous cases separate.

### dherincx92/fpds — maintained async FPDS ATOM parser
- URL: https://github.com/dherincx92/fpds
- Exact commit / revision: `429094dace3ff92ffe710df3dbd9849eae7e6b39`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: watch
- Concrete capability: MIT Python library/CLI that handles FPDS ATOM pagination, XML-to-JSON conversion, query parameter quoting/validation and async iteration; it is the parser used by the Big Local News cancellation pipeline.
- Rare / undernoticed value: A maintained bridge to legacy FPDS transaction semantics remains useful for modification-level evidence and historical edge cases not always convenient through higher-level USAspending products.
- Likely buyer / user: GovCon data teams, procurement analysts, journalists, audit/research pipelines.
- Monetization mechanism: Embedded ingestion component inside award/modification history and cancellation-signal services rather than a standalone product.
- Likely first paid wedge: Use it only for modification/event fields not cleanly exposed by the preferred official USAspending path, then reconcile every record to PIID/transaction evidence.
- Build-time / data advantage: Weeks to 1–2 months of pagination/XML/query handling and tests.
- Evidence inspected: repository metadata/license, current README usage, async request/iteration examples, parameter-validation behavior and performance history; exact revision.
- Public license / rights: MIT. User-asserted separate commercial permission also applies to repository-owned code. FPDS data/source availability remains separately governed.
- Reuse classification: Reusable, but legacy FPDS should be a supplemental transaction source rather than CaptureBrief's primary identity/award authority.
- Combination opportunities: Pair with Big Local News termination taxonomy and USAspending/DATA Act reconciliation; use as an independent regression source for PIID/modification edge cases.
- Value score: A 3/5; B 3/5; C 4/5; D 3/5; E 5/5; F 5/5 = **23/30**.
- Next action: Test the current ATOM feed on a small set of known modification events and compare field completeness/latency with USAspending transaction records before adopting.

### acqagent/rfo-deviations — versioned FAR Overhaul class-deviation corpus
- URL: https://github.com/acqagent/rfo-deviations
- Exact commit / revision: `ccf31107508085cc311fb07488eb513ab97c6b7d`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: strong / Master contender
- Concrete capability: Dated machine-readable snapshots of civilian-agency FAR Overhaul class-deviation PDFs sourced from the official acquisition.gov guide, with a manifest keyed by source URL hash, agency, FAR Part and filename plus per-agency Part 52 workbooks. The latest inspected snapshot records 1,256 PDF/files after manifest cleanup, 1,221 deviations, 1,100 effective dates, 495 Part 52 entries and explicit skipped/404 counts.
- Rare / undernoticed value: It is a ready-made point-in-time corpus of the exact evidence needed to answer 'which agency deviation was published/effective for this FAR part at this date?' while preserving direct official-source links and missing-source accounting. Popular FAR datasets usually expose codified text, not the moving interim deviation layer.
- Likely buyer / user: GovCon compliance/capture teams, acquisition support firms, legal/regulatory intelligence products, proposal consultants.
- Painful problem: Hundreds of agency-issued deviation PDFs change the operational rule surface during the FAR overhaul, and source links can rot. Manual collection/versioning is expensive and error-prone.
- Monetization mechanism: Managed class-deviation monitor; premium CaptureBrief rule-currency evidence; fixed-price solicitation applicability review.
- Likely first paid wedge: Agency + solicitation date + cited FAR clauses -> return all potentially controlling deviation documents, effective-date evidence, source URL/hash and a human-review status.
- Build-time / data advantage: Several months of corpus assembly, versioning, source-link tracking and normalization already compressed into releases/manifests.
- Evidence inspected: exact latest commit metadata; README release/snapshot table, manifest schema, per-agency Part 52 workbook description, exclusions and missing-link caveats; sibling collector provenance.
- Public license / rights: README states federal PDFs are U.S. Government works/public domain under 17 U.S.C. §105 and repository manifest/README/packaging are CC BY 4.0. User's asserted separate commercial permission also covers repository-owned material. Derived workbook/extraction assertions still require verification against source PDFs.
- Reuse classification: Directly useful as an evidence corpus. Treat official PDFs as source authority; treat clause-level workbook mappings and model-derived fields as derived indexes requiring source verification.
- Why non-obvious: Four stars and a dataset/corpus name hide a uniquely current operational-acquisition dataset with direct commercial applicability to proposal compliance.
- Combination opportunities: `acqagent/far-collector` refresh pipeline + this corpus + GSA FAR DITA + mcp-sam-gov prescriptions + fuel-guard/CivicProof-style verification gate.
- Value score: A 4/5; B 5/5; C 5/5; D 5/5; E 5/5; F 5/5 = **29/30**.
- Next action: Materialize a clause/part/agency/effective-date index with source-PDF hashes and supersession relationships; independently verify a sample of per-clause workbook mappings before any automated applicability claim.

### EricGrill/mcp-civic-data — direct SBA open-data size-standard adapter
- URL: https://github.com/EricGrill/mcp-civic-data
- Exact commit / revision: `486e814080d0a4c621eb3dcee997998682eb2c12`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: watch
- Concrete capability: MIT MCP server spanning public government APIs; the inspected SBA module queries the SBA CKAN catalog and the current data.sba.gov Socrata size-standards dataset (`jfx9-jbxa`) directly by NAICS/industry rather than embedding a static table.
- Rare / undernoticed value: The useful part is source choice, not the MCP shell: it demonstrates a simple live authoritative-data path for NAICS size-standard lookups, which is safer than stale hard-coded tables discovered elsewhere.
- Likely buyer / user: GovCon qualification tools, small-business consultants, capture teams.
- Monetization mechanism: Embedded current-size-standard fact retrieval feeding a reviewed eligibility packet.
- Likely first paid wedge: For a target solicitation NAICS, retrieve the current official SBA size-standard row with timestamp/source metadata, then combine it with customer financial/headcount facts and the controlling SBA rule rather than declaring eligibility from the dataset alone.
- Build-time / data advantage: Modest; weeks of source discovery/API plumbing, but not the harder business-affiliation/calculation logic.
- Evidence inspected: repository metadata/license, current commit, `src/mcp_govt_api/tools/sba.py` endpoint/dataset identifiers and filtering/error behavior.
- Public license / rights: MIT for code. SBA open-data contents and current eligibility rules remain separately authoritative government sources. User-asserted commercial permission applies to repo-owned code/content.
- Reuse classification: Reusable adapter; insufficient alone for deterministic small-business eligibility.
- Combination opportunities: Official SBA dataset retrieval + a future verified affiliation/receipts/headcount rule engine + SAM registration/certification evidence + CaptureBrief qualification packet.
- Value score: A 3/5; B 3/5; C 3/5; D 2/5; E 4/5; F 5/5 = **20/30**.
- Next action: Validate the Socrata dataset schema/freshness against SBA's published table and search for an authoritative current affiliation/receipts calculation implementation rather than adding more generic API wrappers.

### dot-org-ai/standards.org.ai — SBA transform with unsafe hard-coded eligibility layer
- URL: https://github.com/dot-org-ai/standards.org.ai
- Exact commit / revision: `32484e22a567406f1e7105fda0e5fb1865eafcfa`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: rejected / deprioritized
- What was inspected: `.scripts/us-sba.ts` transforms size-standard source TSVs into normalized SBA/NAICS records and relationships, but the same file falls back to hand-authored business-type eligibility descriptions and hard-coded set-aside/sole-source thresholds. Those embedded legal/program descriptions are not a safe current eligibility authority.
- Reason not retained: The normalization idea is generic and already dominated by live official SBA-source adapters, while stale/hard-coded program rules could create false qualification conclusions.
- Public license / rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 verified from the repository LICENSE; user separately asserts commercial permission for repository-owned material. External/source datasets remain separately governed.
- Reuse classification: Do not use its hard-coded SBA eligibility/threshold content as rule truth. If reused at all, limit to generic transform architecture and replace facts with versioned authoritative sources.
- Value score: A 1/5; B 2/5; C 2/5; D 2/5; E 1/5; F 5/5 = **13/30**.
- Next action: Do not re-search unless the project replaces hard-coded SBA program logic with sourced/versioned official rules and tests.
